headline: Cancer multi-omics integration moves into survival models, tensors and queryable resources
label: Cancer Multi Omics Integration
summary: New tools couple molecular layers for cancer prognosis, from benchmarked joint reduction and zero-shot pan-cancer survival to tumor PTM and driver databases.
synthesis: The dominant thread is integrating heterogeneous cancer molecular layers for prognosis and interpretation. On the modelling side, HIT-Fuse fuses six omics and pathomics modalities via autoencoders and CP decomposition while handling missing modalities. UniPanSurv uses a shared backbone with a discrete-time hazard head for zero- and few-shot pan-cancer survival. A benchmark of 12 joint dimension reduction methods across 18 TCGA cancer datasets finds JIVE and RGCCA strongest for survival prediction. Pathway-Transformer adds alternative splicing and polyadenylation variants to expression within KEGG pathway structure. On the resource side, DriverDBv5 examines the prognostic weight of multi-omics drivers, PTMlink scores glycosylation–phosphorylation co-variation across 1,211 CPTAC tumors, and PDAC BioPortal unifies bulk, single-nucleus and spatial pancreatic cohorts. Related tooling covers CRISPRi-informed GRN inference in TNBC, pyGENIE for GENIE access, Met4All for methylation arrays and ProReT for program-level drug repurposing. What stands out is the systematic comparison of integration methods against survival endpoints, rather than single-method proposals.
